study_identification.title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate cerebellar damage patterns resulting from brainstem tumors in children and their association with behavioral disorders, using normative modeling to assess individual structural deviations and predict behavioral outcomes.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (72 locally recruited children in Beijing; fcon_1000.projects; Child Connectome Project (CCNP); Children's Hospital in Guangzhou)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: ACAPULCO (Automatic Cerebellum Anatomical Parcellation using U-Net with Locally Constrained Optimization) v0.2.1 with pediatric template; MRIcroGL for brainstem exclusion; ITK-SNAP for manual correction; 26 cerebellar lobule segmentation

quality_checking_detail.answer: Two neurosurgery specialists independently reviewed segmentation quality; manual corrections performed for inaccurately segmented images based on cerebellar lobule anatomical morphology using ITK-SNAP; cases with poor MRI scanning (6 patients, 8 healthy children) excluded; tumors involving cerebellum or thalamus (6 patients) excluded; segmentation issues (10 patients) excluded

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization method utilized to harmonize data from different sources, mitigating non-biological variance from inter-scanner discrepancies; retained age, gender, and TIV as covariates while excluding diagnostic labels

software_tool.answer: Not explicitly stated (likely PCNtoolkit or custom implementation in Python 3.7)

response_variable.answer: Cerebellar lobule volumes (26 regions: left and right lobules I-III, IV, V, VI, VIIB, VIII (merged from VIIIA and VIIIB), IX, X, Crus I, Crus II, and vermis lobules VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, and corpus medullare)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex modeled as covariates in GPR framework (fixed effects implied by GPR implementation)

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study addresses site effects through ComBat harmonization (controlling for mean shifts and variance differences across sites) and includes age, sex, and TIV as covariates. However, the paper does not provide detailed validation of how well the normative model handles nuisance structure comprehensively (e.g., correlation structure, nonlinearity beyond age smoothing in GPR). The GPR approach inherently handles nonlinearity in age effects, and ComBat addresses site-related variance, but explicit validation metrics for these aspects are not reported.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We utilized the Combat method to harmonize data from different sources, mitigating non-biological variance from inter-scanner discrepancies. This method has been validated for effectively reducing unwanted variation introduced by site differences in structure MRI investigations. Notably, this method retained age, gender, and TIV as covariates while excluding diagnostic labels. Using volumetric data from the 26 cerebellar regions, we established normative models with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), incorporating age and gender as covariates. This Bayesian non-parametric modeling approach inherently considers prediction uncertainty and provides probability distributions for predicted values.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study explicitly performed 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy children dataset to estimate model performance before developing the definitive models for deviation analysis. This represents validation using non-independent data within the same domain (training dataset with cross-validation splits).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: We initially estimated models with 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy children dataset, then developed definitive models for deviation analysis in patients.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not report validation of the normative model using an independent hold-out sample from the same domain (healthy children dataset). All healthy children data appear to have been used for training the final normative model after 10-fold cross-validation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: We initially estimated models with 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy children dataset, then developed definitive models for deviation analysis in patients. For each participant, the normative model was used to predict volume estimates for each region, along with corresponding predictive uncertainty.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study applies the normative model to a different domain (patient population with brainstem tumors), which technically constitutes cross-domain application. However, this is the primary analysis rather than a validation exercise. The paper does not report applying the model to an independent healthy children dataset from different sites/scanners to validate generalization. The multi-site nature of the healthy children data (4 different sites) provides some evidence of cross-site generalization within the training phase, but formal external validation on a completely separate healthy cohort is not reported.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Initially, we enrolled 171 pediatric patients diagnosed with brainstem tumors and 849 typically developing children from 4 different sites. To establish a normative model, data from 849 healthy children (age range: 4-18 years) were collected from publicly available databases, including 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 of whom underwent scanning), 69 from the fcon_1000.projects dataset, 450 from the Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from the Children's Hospital in Guangzhou.

clinical_dataset.answer: Beijing Tiantan Hospital pediatric brainstem tumor cohort (147 patients enrolled between April 2019 and December 2022)

diseases_studied.answer: Brainstem tumors (predominantly Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma - DIPG: 78.8%)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score calculated as Z_ij = (y_ij - ŷ_ij) / sqrt(σ_ij^2 + σ_nj^2) where y_ij is true volume, ŷ_ij is expected volume from GPR, σ_ij is predictive uncertainty, and σ_nj is variance from normative distribution; total outlier count (tOC) across 26 regions for volumes below -1.96 (below 2.5th percentile); deviation rate computed by counting patients with Z-values exceeding ±1.96

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Pearson correlation analysis between tOC and behavioral scores (social problems: r=0.31, p=0.001; withdrawal behaviors: r=0.28, p=0.001). Ridge regression model with nested 5-fold cross-validation (101 repetitions) to predict behavioral scores from tOC and from 26 regional volume deviations. Linear regression within each fold to adjust for age and sex effects. Permutation testing (1000 iterations) to assess prediction significance. Feature weights from ridge regression to identify regional contributions (positive weights: larger volumes linked to higher behavioral scores; negative weights: smaller volumes associated with higher scores). Multiple linear regression to explore associations between clinical variables (duration, tumor volume, KPS, symptoms, etc.) and tOC values. Supplementary multiple regression analysis between clinical features and behavioral features.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Over 95% of patients showed negative cerebellar deviations, particularly in anterior lobules; higher tOC significantly correlated with severe social problems (r=0.31, p=0.001) and withdrawal behavior (r=0.28, p=0.001); reduced cerebellar volumes in regions like Right X, V, IV, Left IX, VIII, X, and V predicted worse behavioral outcomes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study revealed widespread cerebellar structural abnormalities in over 95% of brainstem tumor patients, with most pronounced negative deviations in anterior lobules (Left I-V, Right I-V) and vermis cerebelli (Vermis IV-VII). Female patients exhibited higher prevalence of extreme negative deviations compared to males. Tumor volume showed significant positive association with tOC (r=0.41, p<0.001). Total outlier count (tOC) significantly predicted social problems (mean r=0.27, p=0.030) and withdrawal behaviors (mean r=0.25, p=0.034) in 5-fold cross-validation. Cerebellar volume deviations significantly predicted social problems (r=0.27, p=0.007) and withdrawal behaviors (r=0.25, p=0.015). Negative feature weights (indicating smaller volumes associated with worse symptoms) were identified in Right X, Right V, Right IV, Left IX, Left VIII, Left X, Left V, and Right VIIB for social problems, and in Left V, Right IV, Vermis VIII, Left X, Left IV, Left IX, Vermis VI, Right X, Right VIIB, Vermis X, Right Crus I, and Right V for withdrawal behaviors. Regions showing consistent negative associations with both behaviors included Right X, Left X, Right V, Left V, Right IV, and Left IX. The findings emphasize involvement of both anterior motor-associated lobules (IV, V) and posterior cognitive-affective regions (VIII, IX, X, Crus I/II) in behavioral disorders, suggesting distributed cerebellar contributions to social functions. Average tOC was 1.3 (SD=2.0) in patients, with 95% of cases showing tOC values between 3 and 10, while healthy children showed minimal tOC values clustered around zero.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, the normative model included only age and gender, not accounting for education or home environment which might affect brain indices. Second, the behavioral questionnaire (CBCL) focused mainly on general behavioral problems and lacked depth in assessing specific social functions; a more specialized tool is needed. Third, the study found correlation between cerebellar deformation and behavioral disturbances but does not establish causality. Fourth, the study is cross-sectional and cannot assess temporal relationships or developmental trajectories. Fifth, the sample consisted of predominantly DIPG cases (78.8%), which may limit generalizability to other brainstem tumor types.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study creatively uses automated U-Net-based segmentation (ACAPULCO) to analyze detailed cerebellar changes in brainstem tumor patients, providing precise quantification of cerebellar atrophy at the lobular level compared to previous studies that relied on basic measurements. The use of normative modeling reduces clinical and biological variability, enhancing reliability of findings. A key contribution is linking secondary cerebellar damage from brainstem tumors to specific social behavioral patterns with neuroimaging evidence. The tOC metric serves as a quantitative indicator for evaluating cerebellar health at the individual level, potentially informing clinical decision-making. Ridge regression feature weights offer valuable insights for identifying specific cerebellar regions associated with behavioral outcomes in large-scale neuroimaging studies. The findings suggest that protecting cerebellar-brainstem functional circuits could be crucial for preserving patient function and may inform surgical strategies, though further research is needed to validate in clinical practice. The study highlights the role of brainstem-cerebellar circuits in social behaviors and suggests early recognition of cognitive and behavioral disorders may facilitate timely medical intervention.

general_notes.general_notes: This study represents a pioneering effort to link secondary cerebellar changes caused by brainstem tumors to behavioral patterns in pediatric patients using individualized normative modeling. The study addresses an important clinical question about the mechanisms underlying behavioral disorders in brainstem tumor patients, which have historically been understudied compared to motor and neurological symptoms. Full dataset list: 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 underwent scanning), 69 from fcon_1000.projects dataset (https://doi.org/10.15387/fcp_indi.corr.ipcas7), 450 from Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from Children's Hospital in Guangzhou. The study complies with Chinese regulations regarding human genetic resources - all data collected, processed, and stored within China with no transfer of original images to foreign institutions. Ethical approval from IRB of Beijing Tiantan Hospital (Approval No. KY 2019-124-02). The study excluded brainstem region before cerebellar segmentation to avoid misclassification due to tumor-induced brainstem swelling. CBCL behavioral assessment included 113 items categorizing into eight factors: somatic complaints, withdrawal behaviors, depression/anxiety, aggressive behaviors, delinquent behavior, thought problems, and social problems. Statistical analyses conducted in Python 3.7. Code publicly available at: https://github.com/heyuanJ/cerebellum and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15023957. Supplementary data includes source data for figures (Supplementary Data 1), cerebellar segmentation flowchart (Fig. S1), correlation between tOC and tumor volume (Fig. S2), behavioral comparison results (Fig. S3), and effects of clinical features on behaviors (Table S1). Tumor locations: Pons 62.6%, Multi-locations 20.4%, Medulla 8.8%, Midbrain 8.2%. Common symptoms: Limb weakness 57.8%, Ataxia 55.8%, Diplopia 54.4%, Bucking 44.9%, Headache 28.6%, Emesis 28.6%, Dysarthria 25.2%, Dysphagia 16.3%. Mean KPS score 77±10, mean symptom duration 5.4±11.2 months, mean tumor volume 26.97±14.7 cm³. The paper was received on 5 September 2024 and accepted on 17 March 2025, published in Communications Medicine (Nature Portfolio journal).
